indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: Demonstrate understanding of Roman Numerals up to C (i.e. 100)
indicator.objective: Recognize Roman Numerals system up to C (i.e. 100)

skills.description: Convert a Roman numeral (I–C) to a Hindu-Arabic numeral.
Convert a Hindu-Arabic numeral (1–100) to a Roman numeral.
Identify the value of a Roman numeral symbol or explain a simple additive/subtractive combination.

misconceptions: Writing IIII for 4 instead of IV
Using V, L, or C more than once in a numeral

questions.stem: What is VII in Hindu-Arabic numerals?
questions.misconception: Counting symbols instead of using their values.

questions.stem: What is XII in Hindu-Arabic numerals?
questions.misconception: Thinking X = 1 because it is one symbol.

questions.stem: What is XXIV in Hindu-Arabic numerals?
questions.misconception: Reading IV as 6 (adding 1 and 5).

questions.stem: What is XL in Hindu-Arabic numerals?
hints: When a smaller numeral comes before a larger one, subtract.
questions.misconception: Adding 10 + 50 = 60.

questions.stem: What is XCIV in Hindu-Arabic numerals?
questions.misconception: Reading IV as 6 instead of 4.

questions.stem: What is LXXXVII in Hindu-Arabic numerals?
questions.misconception: Counting each symbol as 1 and getting 7.

questions.stem: What is XCIX in Hindu-Arabic numerals?
questions.misconception: Reading IX as 11 (adding) instead of 9 (subtracting).

questions.stem: How do you write 8 in Roman numerals?
questions.misconception: Writing IIX by trying to subtract.

questions.stem: How do you write 15 in Roman numerals?
questions.misconception: Writing VX by putting the smaller symbol first incorrectly.

questions.stem: How do you write 29 in Roman numerals?
questions.misconception: Writing XXVIV by adding V and IV incorrectly.

questions.stem: How do you write 45 in Roman numerals?
questions.misconception: Writing VL by using 5 before 50 incorrectly.

questions.stem: How do you write 76 in Roman numerals?
questions.misconception: Writing LXXIV for 76 (that is 74).

questions.stem: How do you write 88 in Roman numerals?
questions.misconception: Writing LXXXIIX by using subtractive notation for 8.

questions.stem: How do you write 94 in Roman numerals?
questions.misconception: Writing LXXXXIV by using four Xs instead of XC.

questions.stem: What value does the Roman numeral symbol V represent?
hints: V is one of the basic Roman symbols.
It looks like a hand with five fingers.
questions.misconception: Confusing V with X (10).

questions.stem: What value does the Roman numeral symbol L represent?
hints: L is larger than X but smaller than C.
questions.misconception: Confusing L with C (100).

questions.stem: In the numeral IX, why is I placed before X?
options: Because I is always written first
Because X cannot start a numeral
hints: When a smaller symbol comes before a larger one, we subtract.
questions.misconception: Thinking I before X means 1 + 10 = 11.

questions.stem: What value does the Roman numeral symbol C represent?
hints: C is the largest symbol in our range.
C comes from the Latin word for hundred.
questions.misconception: Confusing C with L (50).

questions.stem: Explain why XL = 40.

criteria.description: Explains that a smaller numeral before a larger one means subtraction (50 − 10 = 40)

questions.explanation: X = 10 and L = 50. Since X comes before L, we subtract: 50 − 10 = 40.
questions.misconception: Adding 10 + 50 to get 60.

questions.stem: Which is greater: LXXXIX or XC? Explain your answer.
options: LXXXIX, because it has more symbols
LXXXIX, because L is larger than X
questions.explanation: LXXXIX = 89 and XC = 90, so XC is greater.
questions.misconception: Thinking more symbols always means a larger number.
